title: Existence of compatible alternating injective resolution rows
statement: Let $B$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives]. Let $K$ be a $\mathbb Z$-indexed cochain complex with $K^p=0$ for $p<0$, and let $S$ be its image under the single-degree-zero functor $B\to\operatorname{CochainComplex}(B,\mathbb N)$. There is a compatible row system $R$ for $S$ [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-rows] such that $A^p=0$ for $p<0$, each of $A^p,Z^p,D^p,H^p$ has injective terms, and each of its four augmentations $j_A^p,j_Z^p,j_D^p,j_H^p$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. This asserts only existence of the row system, not any identification with the cycles, images or homology of its associated complex.

source.place: Lemma 015I, proof Steps 1--4; prescribed horseshoe Lemma 013T

proof.text: Form the two alternating short exact sequences of cycles, terms, boundaries and homology.

Start with an injective resolution of Z^0. At each degree choose the free boundary or homology resolution using InjectiveResolution.of; apply the prescribed horseshoe twice, reusing the shared columns. Retain the commuting augmentation squares and the degreewise short exact rows.

Choose zero columns in negative degrees and for D^0, identifying H^0 with Z^0. The hypotheses imply all negative source cycles, boundaries and homology vanish. Prolong the source by the exact single-degree-zero functor. Its canonical cycle/image/homology isomorphisms transport the augmentations, and the horseshoe squares and factorization of d_K give the four compatibility equations.
